extracted.intended_audience: early postdoctoral researchers (biomedical) applying for Helen Hay Whitney Foundation research fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for applicants to the Helen Hay Whitney Foundation three-year postdoctoral research fellowship in basic biomedical sciences. Covers eligibility, review criteria, award conditions, stipend/allowances, and procedural requirements (deadlines, activation, meetings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree timing eligibility (Ph.D. / equivalent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have received a Ph.D. (or D.Phil. or equivalent) degree no more than two years before the application deadline are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'they have received a Ph.D. (or D.Phil. or equivalent) degree no more than two years before the application deadline.' Includes that applicants with a Ph.D. who applied before arriving in their postdoctoral laboratory but did not receive an award are eligible to apply again in the following year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree timing eligibility (M.D. / M.D.-Ph.D.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have received an M.D. (or M.D.-Ph.D.) degree no more than four years before the application deadline are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'or an M.D. (or M.D.-Ph.D.) degree no more than four years before the deadline.' For M.D. applicants the four-year interval should include only clinical training and no more than one year in the postdoctoral laboratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral laboratory tenure limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must have been employed in their postdoctoral laboratory for no more than one year before the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'they have been employed in their postdoctoral laboratory for no more than one year before the application deadline.' Clarification: time spent finishing work in the Ph.D. laboratory does not count against this one year; the 'postdoctoral laboratory' is the lab in which they propose to be appointed as a HHW fellow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and counting of postdoctoral time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time in the Ph.D. laboratory used to finish up work does not count toward the one-year postdoctoral laboratory limit; the one-year period begins upon moving to the postdoctoral laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: if Ph.D. received in January, stayed in Ph.D. lab until end of September, and moved to postdoc lab on October 1, the one year begins on October 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of laboratory encouraged / not same-lab training
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does not ordinarily consider applicants who plan tenure of the fellowship in the laboratory in which they have already received extensive predoctoral or postdoctoral training; a change of laboratory is usually advisable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The aim of the fellowship is to broaden postdoctoral training and experience, and a change of laboratory is usually advisable.' This indicates applicants who would remain in the same lab with extensive prior training are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on awards per supervisor per year
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will not make more than one award per year for training with a given supervisor; if more than one application is received from a single laboratory they will review only one, as chosen by the Chair of the SAC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The Foundation will not make more than one award per year for training with a given supervisor. Should we receive more than one application from a single laboratory, we will review only one, as chosen by the Chair of the SAC, and decline the other(s) administratively.' Heads of laboratories are urged to make this choice for the Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum concurrent fellows per laboratory
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does not support more than two fellows per laboratory at the same time; if awards are made in two successive years to a laboratory, applicants from that laboratory are ineligible in the third year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'We also do not support more than two fellows per laboratory at the same time... applicants from that laboratory are ineligible in the third year.' This is a constraint on lab-level fellowship density.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable training setting (academic only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship training is expected to be obtained in an academic setting; selection of a commercial or industrial laboratory for the training experience is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The Foundation expects that fellowship training will be obtained in an academic setting. The selection of a commercial or industrial laboratory for the training experience is not acceptable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Target career stage — early postdoctoral only
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from established scientists or advanced fellows will not be considered; the fellowships are for early postdoctoral training only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Applications from established scientists or advanced fellows will not be considered. The fellowships are for early postdoctoral training only.' Also notes that clinical house-staff training does not count as 'postdoctoral laboratory training.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship and geographic restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships may be awarded to U.S. citizens planning to work in labs either in the U.S., Canada, or abroad and to foreign citizens for research in laboratories in the U.S. only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Fellowships may be awarded to US citizens planning to work in laboratories either in the US, Canada, or abroad and also to foreign citizens for research in laboratories in the US only.' Expectation that most applicants will reside in North America at time of application; foreign students must obtain appropriate visa documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal review criteria — research plan and evidence of promise
rubrics_metrics.description: The research plan and the evidence, from publications and recommendations, of outstanding scientific promise are the principal criteria for awarding a fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The research plan and the evidence, from publications and recommendations, of outstanding scientific promise are the principal criteria for awarding a fellowship.' This is the core merit rubric for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration — overcoming barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: In some cases, consideration is given to applicants having overcome major barriers to scientific success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'with consideration in some cases of having overcome major barriers to scientific success.' This may factor into discretionary assessments of promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and stages (SAC review and interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scientific Advisory Committee reviews applications in several stages, including interviews for finalists (in person or by Zoom) with a member of the SAC; finalists are notified by early October and award selection occurs after SAC meetings in early November.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording describing timeline: candidates notified of status (interview or decline) by early October; SAC meets in early November and selects awardees; Board of Trustees votes to approve recommended awards usually in January. Interviews are part of finalist evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards / competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of fellowships awarded varies year to year; since 2020 they have awarded between 23 and 25 fellowships from an applicant pool of about 600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'We receive more than twenty times as many applications as we can make awards.' This emphasizes high competitiveness; consequence: the Foundation cannot provide critiques of unsuccessful proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Whitney Fellowship is for a period of three years; one- and two-year fellowships are not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The Whitney Fellowship is for a period of three years, contingent on performance satisfactory to the Foundation’s Scientific Advisory Committee. One and two-year fellowships are not considered.' Duration contingent on satisfactory performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation window and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may activate their fellowship anytime from April 1 through September 1, 2027 (activation-year specific).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'You may activate your fellowship anytime from April 1, through September 1, 2027.' Activation timing affects travel reimbursement/payment schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel expense coverage and reimbursement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation provides funds for travel to the fellowship location at activation for the Fellow and family; does not pay for transportation of household goods; also covers travel expenses for the two-day Annual Fellows Meetings in November; reimbursements require submission of receipts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'These reimbursements are in addition to the annual stipend and research allowance.' Reimbursements paid directly to the Fellow upon submission of expense receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend amounts and research allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend amounts are specified per year (1st year $73,000; 2nd $75,000; 3rd $77,000) and there is a $1,500 annual research allowance remitted to the host institution for the Fellow to use at their discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research allowance: 'to be used at the discretion of the Fellow with no deductions for institutional overhead, registration fees, or taxes.' May be used to help defray health insurance premiums. Payment of research allowance made on activation date and annually thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent Child Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a Dependent Child Allowance of $1,500 per annum for each child; there is no allowance for a spouse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'If a fellowship is awarded and the Fellow advises us that he or she is eligible for the Dependent Child Allowance, we will then request a copy of the birth or adoption certificate(s). Payment of the child allowance will be made on the fellowship activation date, and annually thereafter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment schedule and supplementation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend payments are made semi-annually by the Foundation to the administering institution; fellows in training abroad receive quarterly stipend payments directly. Supplementation of the stipend is permitted but it is not acceptable to hold concurrently a full fellowship from another source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Supplementation of the stipend is permitted. It is not acceptable, however, to hold concurrently a full fellowship from another source.' Also: 'Non-research activities, such as teaching, must not occupy more than 10% of the Fellow’s time.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Fellows Meeting attendance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-day Annual Meeting of Fellows is held in November each year; each third-year Fellow presents their research results and attendance in its entirety is expected as a condition of acceptance of the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Attendance at the meeting in its entirety is expected as a condition of acceptance of the fellowship.' The meeting facilitates scientific interchange and exposure to other biomedical fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission method and deadline strictness
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are to be filled out and submitted online at www.hhwf.org and must be received by the Foundation no later than 5:00pm EST on the stated deadline; late applications will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Applications must be received by The Helen Hay Whitney Foundation no later than 5:00pm EST, June 16, 2026. Late applications will not be considered.' Also: 'Click Here To Apply Online' (online-only submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: No critiques for unsuccessful proposals due to volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the large number of applications, the Foundation cannot provide critiques of unsuccessful proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'We receive more than twenty times as many applications as we can make awards. Because of the large number of applications, we cannot provide critiques of unsuccessful proposals.' This sets applicant expectations about feedback.
